neighbours.label: Modular arithmetic and checksum or hash code: ' modulo', ' modulus', 'finite field', md5 and sha calls; ordinary code and non-maths uses of the words stay low.
fire: The result is taken modulo a large prime.
This code works over a finite field of size two.
We reduce each power modulo seven.
Keep the remainder after dividing by the prime.
The check digit is the remainder after dividing by eleven.
quiet: The result is taken from a large sample.
This code works over a slow network at home.
We multiply each power by seven.
Keep the quotient after dividing by the prime.
The check digit is the sum of the first eleven.

notes: Probes: 0.20-1.01, peaks on the math or hash word. Ordinary code and other uses of 'finite' and 'last' 0.01-0.02, and ' digits' 0.27, so plain arithmetic may read too; three near misses test that. Two fire sentences say it without those words ('remainder after dividing'), which is the meaning-without-word check; they may read low.
